extracted_claims.text: As originally adopted, the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, in force 1 August 2024) set 2 August 2026 as the date from which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply.

The European Commission proposed (via the 'Digital Omnibus on AI') to adjust the timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, so that the rules would start to apply once the Commission confirms that the needed standards and tools are available.
The AI Omnibus amending regulation was adopted on 19 November 2025, a political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026.
Under the AI Omnibus, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply starting 2 December 2027.
Under the AI Omnibus, the obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I apply starting 2 August 2028.

The consolidated text of Article 113 (as in force from 27 July 2026) provides that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (containing the Annex III high-risk requirements), with the exception of Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027.

The amended Article 111(2) provides that, apart from the Article 5 prohibitions, the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2026 only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date.

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27 July 2026) ties the grandfathering rule for already-placed high-risk AI systems to 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113' rather than stating the date directly in the excerpt shown.
Some sources report that the Annex III high-risk deadline was further moved, via a 'second amendment' of Article 113 agreed in September 2026, to 2 August 2029.
Under the claimed 2 August 2029 timeline, providers would not need a conformity assessment by a notified body for Annex III systems until that date.

One source states that high-risk AI obligations were originally expected to become fully applicable 36 months after entry into force of the Act (i.e., around August 2027), rather than 24 months (August 2026).

Several commentary/news sources (published without clear dates or before the Omnibus's final adoption) continue to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations.

Non-compliance with AI Act obligations, including those for high-risk systems, can lead to fines of up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover (or, per an older estimate, up to €35 million) depending on the provision violated.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for obligations covering high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III (medium confidence), but this date was formally postponed to 2 December 2027 through the "Digital Omnibus on AI," which entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence for the entry-into-force fact; high confidence for the new 2 December 2027 application date). A smaller cluster of later, less-authoritative sources claims a further push to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU institution and should be treated with significant caution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024 and set 2 August 2026 as the date from which Annex III high-risk obligations would apply (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). One source states high-risk obligations were originally expected to apply 36 months after entry into force (around August 2027) rather than the commonly cited 24 months (medium confidence), creating a minor discrepancy with the majority view [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would apply only once the Commission confirmed necessary standards and tools were available (medium confidence) [Council and Parliament agree to simplify rules](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). The resulting AI Omnibus amending regulation was adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement reached 7 May 2026, and entry into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

Under this Omnibus, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), corroborated by multiple official EU guidance sources [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation). The consolidated Article 113 text confirms that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (containing Annex III requirements), except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113).

### Grandfathering and Transitional Rules
Amended Article 111(2) provides that, apart from Article 5 prohibitions, the Regulation applies to high-risk systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 only if they undergo significant design changes afterward (medium confidence) [Article 111 AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111). The consolidated EUR-Lex text ties this grandfathering rule to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than a fixed date (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), leaving ambiguity about whether 2 August 2026 still functions as the relevant reference point despite the main deadline shifting to 2027.

### Disputed Further Extension
A small set of sources claims a "second amendment" agreed in September 2026 pushed the Annex III deadline further to 2 August 2029 (high confidence per source scoring, but not institutionally verified) [EU AI Act: Annex III high-risk deadline moved](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update). Under this claimed timeline, notified-body conformity assessments would not be required until 2029 (medium confidence) [When do the AI Act's Annex III rules apply?](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply). No official EU source corroborates this claim.

### Enforcement
Non-compliance with high-risk obligations can result in fines up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, with older estimates citing figures up to €35 million (low confidence) [Goodwin Law Timeline](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- Several commentary sites continue citing 2 August 2026 as operative, apparently predating or overlooking the Omnibus amendment [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), contradicting official guidance confirming 2 December 2027 [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).
- **Flagged — below 0.4 confidence:** none of the core claims fall below this threshold, but the claimed 2 August 2029 extension, while scored at 0.70 for corroboration among its own cluster, rests entirely on non-institutional, speculative sources and conflicts with official sources fixing 2 December 2027 [Client alert](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline).
- Europarl's 36-month timeline claim conflicts with the widely cited 24-month original deadline [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

## Knowledge Gaps
Whether the 2 August 2029 date is an officially adopted amendment remains unconfirmed by any EUR-Lex, Commission, or Council publication. It is also unclear whether the Commission's conditional "standards readiness" mechanism survived into the final Omnibus text or was replaced by the fixed 2 December 2027 date. The precise legal interaction between the Article 111 grandfathering reference to 2 August 2026 and the new 2027 application date requires further clarification, as does the discrepancy in Europarl's 36-month figure.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for obligations covering high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III (high confidence), but this date was formally postponed to 2 December 2027 through the "Digital Omnibus on AI," which entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence). A smaller cluster of later, less-authoritative sources claims a further push to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU institution and should be treated with significant caution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024 and set 2 August 2026 as the date from which Annex III high-risk obligations would apply (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). One source states high-risk obligations were originally expected to apply 36 months after entry into force (around August 2027) rather than the commonly cited 24 months (medium confidence), creating a minor discrepancy with the majority view [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would apply only once the Commission confirmed necessary standards and tools were available (medium confidence) [Council and Parliament agree to simplify rules](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). The resulting AI Omnibus amending regulation was adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement reached 7 May 2026, and entry into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

Under this Omnibus, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), corroborated by multiple official EU guidance sources [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation). The consolidated Article 113 text confirms that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (containing Annex III requirements), except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113).

### Grandfathering and Transitional Rules
Amended Article 111(2) provides that, apart from Article 5 prohibitions, the Regulation applies to high-risk systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 only if they undergo significant design changes afterward (medium confidence) [Article 111 AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111). The consolidated EUR-Lex text ties this grandfathering rule to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than a fixed date (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), leaving ambiguity about whether 2 August 2026 still functions as the relevant reference point despite the main deadline shifting to 2027.

### Disputed Further Extension
A small set of sources claims a "second amendment" agreed in September 2026 pushed the Annex III deadline further to 2 August 2029 (high confidence per source scoring, but not institutionally verified) [EU AI Act: Annex III high-risk deadline moved](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update). Under this claimed timeline, notified-body conformity assessments would not be required until 2029 (medium confidence) [When do the AI Act's Annex III rules apply?](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply). No official EU source corroborates this claim.

### Enforcement
Non-compliance with high-risk obligations can result in fines up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, with older estimates citing figures up to €35 million (low confidence) [Goodwin Law Timeline](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- Several commentary sites continue citing 2 August 2026 as operative, apparently predating or overlooking the Omnibus amendment [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), contradicting official guidance confirming 2 December 2027 [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).
- The claimed 2 August 2029 extension (low confidence, unverified) conflicts with official sources fixing 2 December 2027, and originates only from non-institutional, speculative sources [Client alert](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline).
- Europarl's 36-month timeline claim conflicts with the widely cited 24-month original deadline [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

## Knowledge Gaps
Whether the 2 August 2029 date is an officially adopted amendment remains unconfirmed by any EUR-Lex, Commission, or Council publication. It is also unclear whether the Commission's conditional "standards readiness" mechanism survived into the final Omnibus text or was replaced by the fixed 2 December 2027 date. The precise legal interaction between the Article 111 grandfathering reference to 2 August 2026 and the new 2027 application date requires further clarification, as does the discrepancy in Europarl's 36-month figure.

However, the executive summary states 'medium confidence for the entry-into-force fact' for claim_003, which is actually scored 0.68 (same tier as claim_002 and others labeled 'medium'), consistent — no major issue. Minor inconsistency: claim_008 is high confidence (0.80) per claims but used to support 'medium confidence' leaving ambiguity' framing in the body without flagging that the underlying claim itself is rated high confidence, slightly understating certainty of the tying language itself versus the interpretive ambiguity, which is a separate (medium) interpretive point. This is a subtle blurring of confidence levels between the sourced fact and the interpretive conclusion drawn from it.

executive_summary_accuracy.notes: The executive summary's claims (original 2026 date, Omnibus shift to 2 Dec 2027, entry into force 27 July 2026, and the unverified 2029 claim) are all accurately reflected and elaborated upon in the body.

knowledge_gaps.notes: Knowledge gaps and open issues are clearly and thoroughly stated, mirroring the 'Open Issues' ground truth list, including the unverified 2029 date, the standards-readiness mechanism, Article 111 ambiguity, and the Europarl 36-month discrepancy.

reviews.feedback: Clarify the confidence framing around claim_008/Article 111 grandfathering: the EUR-Lex text itself is rated high confidence (0.80) for stating that the grandfathering rule is tied to 'the date of application of Chapter III,' but the report's interpretive conclusion (that this creates ambiguity about whether 2 August 2026 still functions as a reference point) is a separate, lower-confidence inference. Distinguish these two confidence levels explicitly in the 'Grandfathering and Transitional Rules' section so readers do not conflate the sourced fact's high confidence with the uncertainty of the interpretive conclusion drawn from it.
